title: Why Is the UAE Leaving OPEC? And What Is OPEC Anyway?
speaker: Tom Wilkinson

keywords.def: a group of independent producers who cooperate to control prices or supply in a market
a fixed limit or amount of something that is allowed or necessary
the economic relationship between how much of something is available and how much people want it
the maximum amount that can be produced, held, or processed
the physical systems and facilities that support an economy or industry
to make something steady and prevent sudden rises or falls

sentences.en: The United Arab Emirates has announced that it is leaving OPEC (the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries) after almost sixty years as a member.
sentences.zh: 阿拉伯联合酋长国宣布，在加入石油输出国组织（OPEC）近六十年后，将退出该组织。

sentences.en: Why does this matter? Well, oil is still one of the most important resources in the world.
sentences.zh: 为什么这很重要？嗯，石油仍然是世界上最重要的资源之一。

sentences.en: The price of oil affects how much we pay for petrol, the cost of transporting food, airline tickets, electricity, and much more.
sentences.zh: 油价会影响我们支付的汽油费、运输食品的成本、机票、电费以及更多方面。

sentences.en: When oil prices rise, the economy is also affected.
sentences.zh: 当油价上涨时，经济也会受到影响。

sentences.en: OPEC is one of the most powerful organisations influencing oil prices.
sentences.zh: OPEC是影响油价的最强有力的组织之一。

sentences.en: For decades, this group of oil-producing countries has worked together to control how much oil enters the global market.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，这个产油国集团一直合作控制进入全球市场的石油数量。

sentences.en: But now one of its main members is walking away.
sentences.zh: 但现在，它的一个主要成员国正在退出。

sentences.en: In today’s episode, we’re going to think about a few important questions.
sentences.zh: 在今天的节目中，我们将思考几个重要的问题。

sentences.en: What is OPEC? Why is it often called an “oil cartel”?
sentences.zh: 什么是OPEC？为什么它经常被称为“石油卡特尔”？

sentences.en: Why has the UAE decided to leave? And what could happen next?
sentences.zh: 阿联酋为什么决定离开？接下来可能会发生什么？

sentences.en: And we’ll do all of this while learning come new vocabulary and practicing your English listening comprehension!
sentences.zh: 我们将一边学习一些新词汇，一边练习你的英语听力理解，来完成这一切！

sentences.en: The United Arab Emirates, or the UAE, has announced that it will leave OPEC after nearly 60 years as a member.
sentences.zh: 阿拉伯联合酋长国，简称阿联酋，宣布在作为成员国近60年后将退出OPEC。

sentences.en: The UAE first joined OPEC in the 1960s and has spent the past six decades working with other major oil-producing nations to coordinate their oil production.
sentences.zh: 阿联酋于20世纪60年代首次加入OPEC，在过去的六十年里，它一直与其他主要的产油国合作来协调石油产量。

sentences.en: But now, that relationship is coming to an end.
sentences.zh: 但现在，这种关系即将画上句号。

sentences.en: Economists and politicians, people in the energy industry around the world, are paying attention, close attention, to this news story.
sentences.zh: 经济学家、政治家以及世界各地的能源行业人士都在密切关注这一新闻报道。

sentences.en: I’ll talk more about why the UAE is leaving later in the episode, but one major reason is that they want more “freedom” over their oil production.
sentences.zh: 我稍后会在节目中详细谈谈阿联酋离开的原因，但其中一个主要原因是他们希望对自己的石油产量拥有更多的“自由”。

sentences.en: OPEC members usually need to agree to production limits or production targets.
sentences.zh: OPEC成员国通常需要就产量限制或生产目标达成一致。

sentences.en: They want to control how much oil enters the global market.
sentences.zh: 他们希望控制进入全球市场的石油数量。

sentences.en: This allows them to keep the prices stable or high.
sentences.zh: 这使他们能够保持价格稳定或维持高位。

sentences.en: But the UAE has been investing billions of dollars into increasing its oil production capacity over the past few years.
sentences.zh: 但在过去几年里，阿联酋一直在投资数十亿美元以提高其石油生产能力。

sentences.en: The country now has the ability to produce much more oil than it currently does, and it wants to take advantage of this.
sentences.zh: 该国目前生产石油的能力远超以往，而且他们希望充分利用这一点。

sentences.en: Instead of limiting oil production, the UAE wants to sell more oil internationally, or at least they want the option to sell more.
sentences.zh: 阿联酋没有限制石油产量，而是希望在国际上出售更多石油，或者至少他们希望拥有更多的销售选择权。

sentences.en: The global oil market is already under a lot of pressure.
sentences.zh: 全球石油市场已经承受着巨大的压力。

sentences.en: There are tensions in the Middle East and tensions around the Strait of Hormuz, which I’m sure you all know about.
sentences.zh: 中东地区存在紧张局势，霍尔木兹海峡周边也存在紧张局势，我相信大家都知道这一点。

sentences.en: And this has really disrupted energy supplies and shipping routes.
sentences.zh: 这确实扰乱了能源供应和航运路线。

sentences.en: There are shortages in countries around the world, and oil prices have risen sharply.
sentences.zh: 世界各地的国家都出现了短缺，油价急剧上涨。

sentences.en: Prices usually increase because countries and companies worry about these shortages.
sentences.zh: 由于各国和各大公司对这些短缺感到担忧，价格通常会上涨。

sentences.en: To understand why the UAE’s decision to leave OPEC matters so much, maybe we should talk about what OPEC is to begin with.
sentences.zh: 为了理解阿联酋决定退出OPEC为什么如此重要，也许我们应该先谈谈OPEC究竟是什么。

sentences.en: OPEC stands for the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries.
sentences.zh: OPEC代表石油输出国组织（Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries）。

sentences.en: It is a group of oil-producing countries that work together to coordinate how much oil they produce and sell to the world.
sentences.zh: 它是一个产油国集团，共同合作来协调他们生产并出售给世界的石油数量。

sentences.en: This means they agree, make an agreement to sell the same amount of oil, or an agreement to sell a certain amount of oil.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们达成一致，达成协议出售相同数量的石油，或者达成协议出售一定数量的石油。

sentences.en: OPEC is one of the most influential organizations in the energy industry because oil is essential to our lives.
sentences.zh: OPEC是能源行业中最具影响力的组织之一，因为石油对我们的生活至关重要。

sentences.en: Cars, planes, factories, shipping, plastics, electricity production, all of these things depend on oil.
sentences.zh: 汽车、飞机、工厂、航运、塑料、电力生产，所有这些都依赖于石油。

sentences.en: And because oil is so important, controlling its supply gives oil-producing countries enormous economic and political power.
sentences.zh: 正因为石油如此重要，控制其供应赋予了产油国巨大的经济和政治权力。

sentences.en: OPEC was founded in 1960 by five countries: Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, and Venezuela.
sentences.zh: OPEC于1960年由五个国家创立：伊朗、伊拉克、科威特、沙特阿拉伯和委内瑞拉。

sentences.en: At that time, these oil-producing countries felt frustrated.
sentences.zh: 当时，这些产油国感到沮丧。

sentences.en: They were frustrated that large Western oil companies controlled oil prices and production.
sentences.zh: 他们感到沮丧的是，西方的大型石油公司控制了油价和产量。

sentences.en: The companies were often from places like the USA or the UK or Europe, and they were making huge profits.
sentences.zh: 这些公司通常来自美国、英国或欧洲等地，并且赚取了巨额利润。

sentences.en: But the countries that actually owned the oil, produced the oil, had a much more limited influence.
sentences.zh: 但真正拥有石油、生产石油的国家，影响力却要小得多。

sentences.en: OPEC was created to give the countries, the oil-producing and the oil-exporting countries, more control.
sentences.zh: 创建OPEC是为了让这些国家，即产油国和石油出口国，获得更多的控制权。

sentences.en: The organization had a few different goals.
sentences.zh: 该组织有几个不同的目标。

sentences.en: It wanted to protect the economic interests of oil-producing countries.
sentences.zh: 它希望保护产油国的经济利益。

sentences.en: So for example, they wanted to stabilize oil prices.
sentences.zh: 例如，他们希望稳定油价。

sentences.en: This meant avoid massive rises or unpredictable crashes.
sentences.zh: 这意味着避免大幅上涨或不可预测的崩盘。

sentences.en: It also wanted the member countries to cooperate with each other instead of competing against each other.
sentences.zh: 它还希望成员国之间相互合作，而不是互相竞争。

sentences.en: Over the decades, more and more countries have joined OPEC, and it grew in power.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，越来越多的国家加入了OPEC，其影响力也不断增长。

sentences.en: In the 1970s, the group demonstrated how much influence it had when oil prices rose dramatically during the oil crisis.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪70年代，当石油危机期间油价戏剧性上涨时，该集团展示了它有多大的影响力。

sentences.en: OPEC still controls a significant share of the world’s oil supply, and they have even expanded their influence through something called OPEC Plus.
sentences.zh: OPEC仍然控制着全球石油供应的大部分份额，他们甚至通过所谓的“欧佩克+”（OPEC Plus）扩大了影响力。

sentences.en: OPEC Plus includes non-members. I think it includes Russia, for example.
sentences.zh: OPEC Plus包括非成员国。我想其中例如包括俄罗斯。

sentences.en: These countries cooperate on decisions, even if they’re not officially part of OPEC itself.
sentences.zh: 这些国家在决策上进行合作，即使它们并非OPEC本身的正式成员。

sentences.en: The reason why OPEC is so influential is the principle of supply and demand.
sentences.zh: OPEC之所以如此具有影响力，是因为供求规律。

sentences.en: If countries reduce oil production, there is less oil available on the market, on the global market.
sentences.zh: 如果各国减少石油产量，市场上可用的石油就会减少，也就是在全球市场上。

sentences.en: There’s less oil to buy. This usually causes prices to rise.
sentences.zh: 可供购买的石油变少了。这通常会导致价格上涨。

sentences.en: But if OPEC countries increase their production and release more oil into the market, prices tend to fall.
sentences.zh: 但如果OPEC国家增加产量并向市场释放更多石油，价格往往会下跌。

sentences.en: There’s more oil to buy. By coordinating production levels together, by cooperating, by agreeing how much oil to sell or not sell, OPEC can influence oil prices.
sentences.zh: 可供购买的石油变多了。通过共同协调生产水平、通过合作、通过商定销售或不销售多少石油，OPEC可以影响油价。

sentences.en: And this is why people sometimes describe OPEC as an “oil cartel “.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么人们有时将OPEC描述为“石油卡特尔”。

sentences.en: Actually, in a lot of the news articles about this story, about the UAE leaving OPEC, the word “cartel” is used.
sentences.zh: 实际上，在许多关于这个故事——即阿联酋退出OPEC——的新闻报道中，都使用了“卡特尔”这个词。

sentences.en: The BBC headline, for example, was: “United Arab Emirates to Quit Oil Cartel OPEC.”
sentences.zh: 例如，BBC的头条新闻是：“阿拉伯联合酋长国将退出石油卡特尔OPEC。”

sentences.en: If you have heard the word “cartel” before, it’s most likely in a negative sense.
sentences.zh: 如果你以前听过“卡特尔”这个词，它很可能是在负面意义上被提及的。

sentences.en: I think the word sounds negative because it is associated with drug cartels.
sentences.zh: 我认为这个词听起来很负面，因为它与贩毒集团（drug cartels）联系在一起。

sentences.en: In economics, though, a cartel is just a group of independent producers, producers of something.
sentences.zh: 然而，在经济学中，卡特尔只是一群独立的生产者，某种产品的生产者。

sentences.en: And these independent producers work together, cooperate with each other, to control prices or control the supply of their product in a market.
sentences.zh: 这些独立的生产者一起工作、互相合作，来控制价格或控制其产品在市场上的供应。

sentences.en: Businesses normally compete against each other.
sentences.zh: 企业通常相互竞争。

sentences.en: But in a cartel, the businesses work together instead of competing.
sentences.zh: 但在卡特尔中，企业是合作而不是竞争的。

sentences.en: This is because sometimes cooperation, working together, can actually earn you more money.
sentences.zh: 这是因为有时候合作，即共同工作，实际上可以为你赚取更多钱。

sentences.en: OPEC fits this definition because its member countries coordinate how much oil they produce.
sentences.zh: OPEC符合这个定义，因为其成员国会协调各自的石油产量。

sentences.en: Instead of every country producing as much oil as possible and then selling as much oil as possible, they agree to limits or they agree to targets.
sentences.zh: 它们不是让每个国家都尽可能多地生产石油然后尽可能多地出售石油，而是同意限制产量或设定目标。

sentences.en: They do this to keep oil prices higher than they would be otherwise.
sentences.zh: 他们这样做是为了使油价保持在比原本更高的水平。

sentences.en: If everyone was just selling as much oil as possible every day, the prices of oil would be lower.
sentences.zh: 如果每个人每天都在尽可能多地卖油，油价就会更低。

sentences.en: But OPEC wants to keep the prices higher, of course.
sentences.zh: 但OPEC当然希望保持更高的价格。

sentences.en: So they agree to produce less oil. I guess the most well-known use of the word cartel is to do with drug cartels.
sentences.zh: 因此他们同意减产。我想这个词最广为人知的用法是与贩毒集团有关。

sentences.en: Drug cartels are illegal criminal organizations involved in violence, smuggling, and crime.
sentences.zh: 贩毒集团是涉及暴力、走私和犯罪的非法犯罪组织。

sentences.en: OPEC, though, is a legal international organization made up of governments.
sentences.zh: 然而，OPEC是由各国政府组成的合法国际组织。

sentences.en: Its meetings are public. Its policies are officially announced.
sentences.zh: 它的会议是公开的。它的政策是官方宣布的。

sentences.en: And its negotiations are relatively open.
sentences.zh: 而且它的谈判相对公开。

sentences.en: But, critics of OPEC do argue that the organization, that OPEC, controls prices too much, and it gives these small countries too much influence.
sentences.zh: 但是，OPEC的批评者确实认为该组织（即OPEC）对价格的控制太多了，这赋予了这些小国太多的影响力。

sentences.en: Let’s go back to the UAE. Why exactly has the UAE decided to leave OPEC?
sentences.zh: 让我们回到阿联酋。阿联酋究竟为什么决定离开OPEC？

sentences.en: The decision seems to be a combination of different things.
sentences.zh: 这个决定似乎是多种因素结合的结果。

sentences.en: Importantly though, the UAE is not the first country to leave OPEC.
sentences.zh: 不过重要的是，阿联酋并不是第一个退出OPEC的国家。

sentences.en: I think Angola, Ecuador, and Qatar have all left in the past, and they have left for similar reasons to the UAE.
sentences.zh: 我想安哥拉、厄瓜多尔和卡塔尔过去都曾离开过，它们离开的原因与阿联酋相似。

sentences.en: But the UAE is the most influential or the largest country to do so recently.
sentences.zh: 但阿联酋是近期采取这一行动的最具影响力或规模最大的国家。

sentences.en: One major factor behind the UAE leaving is freedom, freedom to produce oil.
sentences.zh: 阿联酋退出的一个主要因素是自由，即生产石油的自由。

sentences.en: As we discussed earlier, OPEC works by coordinating oil production among members.
sentences.zh: 正如我们之前讨论的那样，OPEC通过协调成员国之间的石油生产来运作。

sentences.en: Countries agree to limit the amount of oil they produce, or they agree to quotas on oil production, and this is to control the supply and influence prices.
sentences.zh: 各国同意限制其生产的石油数量，或者同意石油生产配额，这是为了控制供应并影响价格。

sentences.en: But these limits, limit how much oil a country can sell, and the UAE seems unhappy with these restrictions.
sentences.zh: 但这些限制限制了一个国家可以出售多少石油，阿联酋似乎对这些限制感到不满。

sentences.en: The UAE seems to want to sell more oil than OPEC allows it to.
sentences.zh: 阿联酋似乎希望出售比OPEC允许的更多的石油。

sentences.en: They want more flexibility to export more oil.
sentences.zh: 他们希望拥有更大的灵活性来出口更多石油。

sentences.en: They no longer want to be tied to those agreements that stop it selling oil when it wants to sell oil.
sentences.zh: 他们不再希望被那些在他们想卖油时阻止他们卖油的协议所束缚。

sentences.en: Another reason is that the UAE has massively increased the amount of oil it can produce.
sentences.zh: 另一个原因是阿联酋大幅增加了其石油开采量。

sentences.en: It’s increased its capacity. They have invested billions of dollars into new infrastructure: new pipelines, new ports, and export sites.
sentences.zh: 它增加了产能。他们已经向新基础设施投资了数十亿美元：新管道、新港口和出口基地。

sentences.en: The UAE is now capable of producing far more oil than it could in the past.
sentences.zh: 阿联酋目前生产石油的能力远远超过了过去。

sentences.en: But the country cannot use this infrastructure or technology fully if they stay in OPEC.
sentences.zh: 但如果留在OPEC，该国就无法充分利用这些基础设施或技术。

sentences.en: Also, not all oil-producing countries want the same thing.
sentences.zh: 此外，并非所有产油国的诉求都完全相同。

sentences.en: For example, countries like the UAE have been in a disagreement with countries like Saudi Arabia.
sentences.zh: 例如，像阿联酋这样的国家与沙特阿拉伯等国一直存在分歧。

sentences.en: Saudi Arabia prefers higher oil prices. They support limiting the oil supply.
sentences.zh: 沙特阿拉伯更喜欢较高的油价。他们支持限制石油供应。

sentences.en: If there is less oil being sold, the prices of oil will be higher, which increases the profit you can make from each barrel of oil you sell.
sentences.zh: 如果出售的石油减少，油价就会更高，这会增加你从销售的每一桶油中获得的利润。

sentences.en: But the UAE seems to be thinking a bit differently.
sentences.zh: 但阿联酋的想法似乎有些不同。

sentences.en: They seem to want to sell more oil right now, even if that makes the price of oil a little bit lower.
sentences.zh: 他们现在似乎想要出售更多的石油，即使这会让油价稍微降低一点。

sentences.en: Possibly this is because they’re nervous about the future of oil.
sentences.zh: 这可能是因为他们对石油的未来感到紧张。

sentences.en: If the world starts using more green energy, if electric cars become dominant around the world, perhaps there’ll be less need for oil.
sentences.zh: 如果世界开始使用更多的绿色能源，如果电动汽车在世界各地占主导地位，也许对石油的需求就会减少。

sentences.en: And the UAE wants to sell its oil right now.
sentences.zh: 而阿联酋现在就想把油卖出去。

sentences.en: And the UAE is becoming much closer to the United States.
sentences.zh: 而且阿联酋与美国的关系正变得越来越密切。

sentences.en: The US is a massive oil-producing country.
sentences.zh: 美国是一个庞大的产油国。

sentences.en: It’s not in OPEC. And it always criticizes OPEC.
sentences.zh: 它不在OPEC之内。并且它总是批评OPEC。

sentences.en: The UAE moving away from OPEC could make the relationship with the US stronger.
sentences.zh: 阿联酋疏远OPEC可能会使它与美国的关系更加牢固。

sentences.en: So at the beginning of May, the UAE announced it was leaving OPEC.
sentences.zh: 所以在5月初，阿联酋宣布退出OPEC。

sentences.en: What could happen? In the short term, we might not notice much of an impact.
sentences.zh: 可能会发生什么？在短期内，我们可能不会注意到太大的影响。

sentences.en: The global oil market is already a mess.
sentences.zh: 全球石油市场已经一团糟。

sentences.en: It’s being influenced heavily by things happening in the Middle East.
sentences.zh: 它正受到中东发生的事情的严重影响。

sentences.en: There are wars and sanctions happening, tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, and that’s affecting prices far more than the UAE leaving would affect it.
sentences.zh: 那里正在发生战争和制裁，霍尔木兹海峡也存在紧张局势，这些对价格的影响远比阿联酋退出的影响要大。

sentences.en: But over the long term, there could be consequences, big consequences.
sentences.zh: 但从长远来看，可能会产生后果，重大的后果。

sentences.en: OPEC’s power depends on cooperation. It works when the members follow production targets together.
sentences.zh: OPEC的力量取决于合作。当成员国共同遵循生产目标时，它才能发挥作用。

sentences.en: The UAE leaving makes them less effective.
sentences.zh: 阿联酋的退出使其效率降低。

sentences.en: The UAE is not the largest oil producer in OPEC, that is Saudi Arabia, but it is a wealthy, influential country producing a lot of oil.
sentences.zh: 阿联酋并不是OPEC中最大的产油国，最大的产油国是沙特阿拉伯，但它是一个富裕、有影响力且生产大量石油的国家。

sentences.en: If the the UAE starts to sell even more oil, that could make oil prices lower over time.
sentences.zh: 如果阿联酋开始出售更多的石油，随着时间的推移，这可能会导致油价下跌。

sentences.en: Might be a good thing for consumers. There is another possibility, though.
sentences.zh: 这对消费者来说可能是件好事。不过，还有另一种可能性。

sentences.en: Oil markets might become less stable. If OPEC countries don’t coordinate together or if there are less countries in OPEC, it could make prices change quicker.
sentences.zh: 石油市场可能会变得不太稳定。如果OPEC国家不进行联合协调，或者OPEC内部国家减少，这可能会导致价格变化更快。

sentences.en: Higher energy prices will mean higher transportation costs.
sentences.zh: 更高的能源价格将意味着更高的运输成本。

sentences.en: Ships, lorries, planes, all of these things will become more expensive.
sentences.zh: 轮船、货车、飞机，所有这些东西都会变得更加昂贵。

sentences.en: The fact that these are more expensive means that consumers, people like us, will have to pay higher food prices or higher prices for services.
sentences.zh: 这些成本的提高意味着消费者——像我们这样的人——将不得不支付更高的食品价格或更高的服务价格。

sentences.en: And there is a possibility that there could be a little bit of a domino effect.
sentences.zh: 而且有可能产生一点多米诺骨牌效应。

sentences.en: If the UAE leaves OPEC successfully and benefits economically, maybe other countries will decide to do the same in the future.​
sentences.zh: 如果阿联酋成功退出OPEC并在经济上受益，也许其他国家未来也会效仿。

sentences.en: OPEC is one of the world’s most powerful energy organizations.
sentences.zh: OPEC是世界上最强大的能源组织之一。

sentences.en: It is made up of countries that influence global oil production and prices.
sentences.zh: 它由影响全球石油产量和价格的国家组成。

sentences.en: But now the UAE has decided to leave. The UAE wants more freedom to produce and sell oil.
sentences.zh: 但现在阿联酋决定退出。阿联酋希望获得更多生产和销售石油的自由。

sentences.en: And while the impact might be limited right now because of the instability in global energy markets, the long-term consequences could be much larger.
sentences.zh: 虽然由于全球能源市场的不稳定性，目前的影响可能有限，但长期的后果可能会大得多。

sentences.en: Decisions made by oil-producing countries affect inflation, transportation, food prices, and our everyday lives.
sentences.zh: 产油国做出的决定会影响通货膨胀、交通运输、食品价格以及我们的日常生活。

sentences.en: What do you think? Do you think countries should cooperate to control prices of things like oil?
sentences.zh: 你怎么看？你认为各国应该合作控制像石油这样的东西的价格吗？

sentences.en: Or do you think they should compete in the market?
sentences.zh: 还是你认为他们应该在市场上竞争？

sentences.en: Have a competition? Is OPEC good for the economy?
sentences.zh: 进行竞争？OPEC对经济有利吗？

sentences.en: Or is OPEC bad for the economy? Would you personally prefer stable energy prices even if they’re a little bit higher?
sentences.zh: 还是说OPEC对经济有害？你个人更喜欢即使稍微高一点但也稳定的能源价格呢？

sentences.en: Or would you prefer cheaper energy prices that could go up and down unpredictably?
sentences.zh: 还是更喜欢可能会不可预测地上下波动的更便宜的能源价格？
